claim: To support them, the German Research Foundation in late 2025 set up a program, with a budget of $35 million, to provide a safe haven for permanently storing copies of U.S. data from public and open sources.
label: TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-13 - not yet checked by the human annotator] The DFG called its 'Förderinitiative ... Datenresilienz 2025 bis 2027' at the end of October 2025 (the call date read only as a search excerpt; WinFuture, 2 Nov 2025: funding 'für den Zeitraum von 2025 bis voraussichtlich 2027' to bring data back from foreign repositories and clouds). The money: 'Die Bundesregierung stellt rund 30 Millionen Euro für die Sicherung wichtiger Forschungsdatenbestände zur Verfügung', awarded through the DFG (Bundestag hib 49/2026, 21 Jan 2026; heise, 22 Jan 2026). EUR 30M is within rule 2 of $35M at any rate from 1.06 to 1.29 $/EUR. Borderline: the call names repositories abroad in general, not only U.S. data (its funded projects are mostly U.S.), and the budget is the federal government's, stated in January 2026.
